fix_history: Fix 1: Renamed getter/metric function suffix from invalid 8-char '6cb98ce3' to valid 32-char MD5 '5e9f703dc627e70a3b4d09452ec3d3ab' (computed from 'edb61b14-a854-4bf5-a075-c8075c11293a|2'). Updated evaluator.func, evaluator.result.type, both function files.
Fix 2: Getter - replaced fragile 'PlaceHolder 1' in shape.name check with slide.shapes.title for reliable title placeholder identification.
Fix 3: Getter - walk up to paragraph-level italic (para.font.italic) when run.font.italic is None, to handle inherited italic formatting.

Fix 4: Getter - aggregate all non-empty runs across all paragraphs instead of returning on first run; report font_name from first non-None value; report italic=True only if all runs resolved to True, False if any is explicitly False, else None.
Fix 5: Metric - explicit True-only check for italic when expected is True, avoiding false positives from None (unresolved inherited italic).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads 24_8.pptx from /home/user/Desktop/ and uses python-pptx to inspect the last slide (prs.slides[-1]).
Getter uses slide.shapes.title (fix #2) for robust title placeholder identification, replacing the previous fragile 'PlaceHolder 1' name check.
Getter aggregates all non-empty runs across all paragraphs (fix #4), ensuring comprehensive coverage of the title text frame.
Getter resolves italic by walking up to paragraph-level (fix #3) when run.font.italic is None, handling inherited italic formatting.
Metric checks both font_name == 'Times New Roman' (0.5 pts) and italic == True (0.5 pts), covering all instruction requirements with partial credit.
Metric requires italic to be explicitly True (not None) to award italic points (fix #5), preventing false positives from unresolved inherited italic.
Expected values {font_name: 'Times New Roman', italic: true} precisely match both requirements in the instruction.
Initial state (Calibri, non-italic) would fail both checks, ensuring negative-control resistance.

Minor residual risk: if italic is only set at slide-master/layout level (not run or paragraph level), both run and paragraph italic would be None causing a false negative. This is unlikely when a user explicitly applies italic via the LibreOffice UI.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: If false negatives from master-level italic inheritance become a concern, consider also walking up to the slide layout or master font.italic as a last fallback before returning None.
